items.entity: 40×20×8 design domain – mapping of element counts to x/y/z (span/height/depth)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says 'problem size is 40×20×8 elements' and never says which count goes with which axis. The paper's y is the vertical/build axis (Fig. 2(a), Eq. 12, Sec. 3.4), and the top3d-derived solver suggests nelx×nely×nelz order. However, Sec. 4.2 splits the 1.5× refined version of this problem (Fig. 5, same BCs, 4×5400 = 21,600 voxels ≈ 60×30×12) 'evenly in the y-direction' into 4 batches. That split is only even if y is the 40- or 8-element direction, not the 20-element one.
readings: x = 40 (span), y = 20 (height), z = 8 (depth) – top3d nelx×nely×nelz order
x = 40 (span), y = 8 (height), z = 20 (depth)
y = 40 (span along the paper's vertical axis), x = 20, z = 8

items.entity: Physical dimensions of the domain / element edge length
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only element counts, with no physical lengths or element size. Sec. 3.4 normalizes the NN input coordinates to [-0.5, 0.5] along the longest edge, but this does not fix the FE element size.
readings: unit cubic elements (domain 40 × 20 × 8 length units)
domain scaled so the longest edge = 1 (1 × 0.5 × 0.2, element size 0.025)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says the NN and SIMP runs use 'the same cantilever beam boundary condition'. The supported region is shown only in Fig. 3(a) ('Boundary condition'), and the text never says which nodes are fixed. Sec. 4.2 reuses these BCs for Fig. 5 without describing them.
readings: all nodes of one full 20×8 end face (x = 0) – top3d default cantilever
only a sub-region of the end face (e.g., a central patch or its edge lines)

items.entity: Constrained DOFs at the fixed end
items.description: No text says which displacement components are restrained. 'Cantilever' suggests a full clamp, but the only specification is Fig. 3(a).
readings: fully clamped: ux = uy = uz = 0 at all support nodes
partial restraint (e.g., ux and uy fixed, uz free / roller-type)

items.entity: Location of the applied load on the free end
items.description: The load location is not described anywhere in the text (Sec. 4.1, Sec. 4.2). It appears only in Fig. 3(a).
readings: bottom edge of the free-end face (x = L, y = 0, all z) – top3d default
mid-height line of the free-end face (x = L, y = H/2, all z)
centre point of the free-end face (x = L, y = H/2, z = W/2)
bottom-centre node of the free end (x = L, y = 0, z = W/2)

items.description: The text does not say whether the load is a single nodal force, a line load across the depth (or how it is shared among nodes), or a traction on a face. Only Fig. 3(a) shows it.
readings: single concentrated nodal force
line load across the full depth with equal force at every node (top3d style)
line load with consistent nodal weights (half force at the two end nodes)
uniform traction over the free-end face or a patch of it

items.description: The text gives no load direction; only Fig. 3(a) does. Because the axis mapping of 40×20×8 is also unstated, the transverse force could act along either cross-section dimension.
readings: transverse along the 20-element dimension (-y, strong-axis bending; top3d default)
transverse along the 8-element dimension (weak-axis / out-of-plane bending)

items.description: No force value is given, yet the reported c = 40.6 (NN) and 37.8 (SIMP) depend on it. The loss (Eq. 20) divides by c0, so the optimization itself is not affected.
readings: -1 at each loaded node (top3d; e.g., total 9 over a 9-node edge)
total force 1 shared over the loaded nodes
single unit point load

items.description: Eq. 20 (Sec. 3.5) uses V* as the equality target and to define c0, but no value is given for the Fig. 3 cantilever (or for any example in the paper).
readings: 0.3 (top3d default)

items.description: Eq. 6 (Sec. 3.2) uses E0 for solid material, but the text only says the material is isotropic.
readings: E0 = 1 (non-dimensional, top3d default)
a physical value, e.g., 200 GPa (steel) or ~2 GPa (polymer)

items.description: Sec. 3.2 states an isotropic linear-elastic material but never gives ν.
readings: 0.3 (top3d default)

items.description: Eq. 6 contains E_min, but no value is given anywhere.
readings: E_min = 1e-9·E0 (top3d default)
E_min = 1e-6·E0
E_min = 1e-3·E0

items.description: Eq. 6 applies ρ^p in both the NN and the SIMP runs (Sec. 3.2), but neither p nor any continuation scheme is stated.
readings: p = 3 fixed (top3d default)
p raised by continuation (e.g., 1 → 3) over the 300 iterations
higher value, e.g., p = 4 fixed or continued beyond 3

items.entity: Density/sensitivity filter and projection (especially the SIMP baseline, Fig. 3(c))
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the NN 'prevents checkerboard patterns without needing filtering', which implies no filter for the NN run. It does not say whether the SIMP baseline used a filter, of what type or radius, or any Heaviside projection. The top3d example uses a density filter with rmin = 1.5.
readings: no filter in either run
SIMP run with density filter, rmin = 1.5 (top3d)
SIMP run with sensitivity filter, rmin = 1.5
SIMP run with a larger radius (rmin ≈ 2–3) and/or Heaviside projection

items.description: Sec. 3.1 describes the first layer as TF 'RandomFourierFeatures' with a 'uniformly sampled kernel', kernels 'initialize[d] in a linear 3D grid', and a 'shift-invariant Gaussian kernel'. It never gives the number of features or grid size, the kernel scale/bandwidth, whether the kernel is trainable, or the dense-layer initialization. These set the NN's implicit minimum length scale.
readings: 5×5×5 = 125 features, TF default Gaussian scale √(3/2)
one feature per element (40×20×8 = 6400)

items.entity: Optimizer hyper-parameters (SGD for 100 iterations, then Adam to 300)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the optimizer sequence and iteration counts, presumably for both runs. Learning rates, SGD momentum and Adam β parameters are not given.
readings: Keras defaults: SGD lr 0.01 (no momentum), then Adam lr 0.001
SGD lr 0.01, then Adam lr 0.01
SGD lr 0.1 with momentum 0.9, then Adam lr 0.01

items.description: Sec. 3.5: α1 starts at 0 and is 'gradually increase[d] every iteration' up to a maximum of 100, but the increment or law is not given. So it is undetermined how closely the design meets V* within 300 iterations and what path it takes.
readings: linear ramp 0 → 100 over the 300 iterations (+1/3 per iteration)
small fixed increment (e.g., +0.05 to +0.1 per iteration), so 100 is never reached
fast ramp reaching the cap of 100 within the first ~100 iterations

items.entity: Design-variable parameterization of the SIMP baseline
items.description: Sec. 4.1: the SIMP baseline is a one-layer network with constant input 1 and one output per element that 'just store[s] the optimization variables', 'similar to the print angle network'. The text does not say whether the outputs go through a sigmoid (as in Eq. 1) or are used directly as densities with bounds or clipping.
readings: ρ_e = sigmoid(w_e)
ρ_e = w_e, clipped to [0, 1] (or [ρ_min, 1]) after each update

items.description: Sec. 3.5 computes c0 on a uniform-V* field. The initial values of the SIMP variables and the initial NN dense weights and biases (and so the NN's starting density field) are not given.
readings: uniform ρ = V* in all elements
uniform ρ = 0.5 (zero pre-sigmoid weights)
Keras default random initialization of the dense layer (non-uniform initial field)
